newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to help Zaire political solution - Mandela.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to help Zaire political solution - Mandela.

text.p: South African officials will go to Tanzania on Thursday to assess how Pretoria can contribute to end violence in Central Africa, President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday.
"They will not only consider the military question, but political solutions as well," Mandela told reporters.
He said the group, including government officials and senior military officers, would find out exactly what was required from South Africa.
The president earlier said he was prepared to send troops to Central Africa as part of an international force, but needed more information to decide how many to commit.

"The army can be trained for anything. We are not the only country who will be contributing to the peace force. We will be acting jointly with countries from the Great Lakes region and other countries like Canada," Mandela said.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali has said he expected more than 12 countries to provide troops and equipment for the force to open up aid routes to starving Rwandan and Burundian refugees in Zaire.
Thousands of the refugees have fled Zaire by lake and land to Tanzania.

The United States and Britain said on Wednesday they were prepared to contribute troops to a multinational force in Zaire. France, Spain and some other countries had announced their readiness earlier.
